fixed.how:
Parser (packages/commands/src/intent.ts, matchAddTask):
- A separator is a colon, a comma, or a dash with a space before it. The same rule applies to taskTitleOf's 'there:' strip.
- A target is a project only when the new projectsNamedBy (commands/shared.ts) finds exactly one. It matches the id, the whole name, or words held whole or from a word's start in one name. It never matches by word overlap.
- Any other words stay the task's own, as before the area: the task is added at once with Undo.
- Only a pronoun ('there', 'it', 'dort') with no project named in this conversation and two or more projects asks. With one project the pronoun, and 'open it', mean that project.

Agent (conversation/agent.ts): when the turn just before asked a parser question with options and this line is one of them (a project's name alone), the agent parses the line that asked again with namedProjectId set to that project. There is no model call. It reads the question from the conversation's rows, so the press also works after a restart.

The fake daemon plays the target, the question and the press. Docs: commands.md, runtime.md, user-guide.

claims.ts gains CLARIFIES, judged before every question pattern of ASKS:
- A question that asks which, who or where (anywhere in it), or starts with what, when or how.
- A question that offers a choice with 'or'. Not 'or not', 'or leave it' or 'or keep it'.
- German: welche, wer, wo, wohin and 'oder' (not 'oder nicht').

A 'needs your yes' sentence beside clarifying questions only is free too. A yes asked in words ('Shall I set …?', '… or not?') stays an asks claim. ADR 0114's amendment of 2026-11-22, runtime.md and user-guide are updated.

not_done.problem: Review non-blocking: withoutAppMarkers is case-sensitive, so 'the app did: …' in lower case passes through.
not_done.why: Kept on purpose. A lower-case 'what the app did: …' inside a sentence is the model's own prose, and it is never drawn as the app's line. Case-insensitive stripping would cut the rest of such a line. Not a marker on screen, so no security gap.

new_problems: Before this area, the parser asked 'No project named "X". Which project?' or '"X" matches several.' for 'switch to X'. Pressing an option there still sends the bare name to the chat model, which is a paid call. The new press path re-parses the asked line with namedProjectId, which finishes only pronoun lines. A line about a name falls back to today's reading. Evidence: agent.ts (the parse block); intent.ts project() and projectIdFor().

namedProjectId is the registry's active project whenever an earlier turn of this conversation switched (agent.ts, where CommandTurn is built). Example: the person switches to Site in chat, then picks Atlas in the header. 'there' in the same chat then means Atlas, not the Site the conversation named. This is the reviewer's non-blocking point, still open. The fix would read the last project.switch change's target (its change log row) instead of the registry.

A turn whose reply is a parser question still shows 'Make this a task' under the person's line ('add a task there: write the FAQ', bench step 05). Its reply has no actions, so isOwnRequest offers it. The link predates this area.
notes_for_other_areas: projectsNamedBy(projects, words) (packages/commands/src/commands/shared.ts) is the strict match for a target named in a line. It matches the id or the whole name, or words held whole or from a word's start in one name. It never matches by word overlap, and never when the words hold more than the name. matchAddTask uses it; matchProjects is unchanged for other commands.

The option pressed under a parser question: when the turn just before has reply.question with options and no actions, and this line is one of the options and names an active project, ConversationAgent re-parses that turn's human.text with CommandTurn.namedProjectId set to the project. The change's wordsUsed is the line that asked. It is read from the conversation rows, so it also works after a restart.

CLARIFIES (packages/runtime/src/conversation/claims.ts) is judged before every question pattern of ASKS: which, who or where anywhere in the question; what, when or how as its first word; or a choice with 'or' / 'oder' (not 'or not', 'or leave it', 'oder nicht'). Any new ASKS pattern inherits it.

Conversation.tsx folds a reply that is its changes' sentences plus whole sentences more into the last change line, before its Undo. A daemon reply that adds a clause to a change sentence ('… This chat stays about Notes.') no longer doubles the change line.

Suggested UPDATE-LOG addition (the session lead writes it): 'l4-chat-answers fixup: "add a task to …" adds there only when the words name a project ("re-check", "fix the login: …" stay the task, at once with Undo); only "there" or "it" with several projects asks "Which project: Notes or Site?", and the button pressed adds there with no model call; a clarifying question from chat is never replaced; a switch said in another project's Chat shows once with its Undo.'
Suggested design note (core-experience §3.9, session lead): chat asks only for a pronoun with nothing named ('Which project: Notes or Site?'), and the option pressed finishes the line that asked.
